agent_note: SPLIT, structurally explained. 30 event quotes: 19 present (63.3%) / 11 past (36.7%). Both tenses well above 25%, so this is a SPLIT_REVIEW case, and the cause is identifiable rather than uncertainty. Two strands are visible in the text: (a) third-person PAST scene narration - q06376, q06378, q06395, q06406, q06416, q06421, six quotes with named characters, past verbs and past dialogue tags; and (b) a first-person PRESENT epistolary strand, which is itself dual in the METHODOLOGY sense - writing-moment present (q06385 'here I am writing another email', q06409 'And now I just feel') plus past recounting inside the same letters (q06369, q06403, q06419, q06361). So both the 'strand' row and the 'dual - epistolary' row apply; that is a finding, not a failure to decide. NOT in the 70-85% present band, so no threshold-gap flag. NO SINGLE QUOTE FLIPS THE LABEL - at 19/11 the nearest single reclassification (q06404 gnomic to event/present, or q06370/q06386 present to past) moves the split by ~3 points and changes nothing. The label is instead sensitive to a whole CLASS of judgments: untagged first-person present passages, which could be epistolary narration (event) or the book's unmarked dialogue (non-diagnostic). I resolved these toward narration on in-text evidence: this book's demonstrable speech (q06407, q06421, q06425, q06373, q06394) always carries 'she said' / 'he answered' tags, whereas the present passages carry none and show written register (dash asides, sustained length, explicit 'writing another email' / 'in case you're worrying about me'). If that entire class were instead ruled dialogue, the present count would collapse and the book would read as past - that is the real risk here and it should be audited. 31 of 68 quotes are gnomic, the highest proportion I would expect anywhere: the Goodreads page for this title is dominated by present-tense essayistic and political generalization, exactly the adversarial false-present bias METHODOLOGY describes. A two-bucket filter would score this book near-100% present.
